thread:
ellie-support: bumping this into eng-runtime — ACME reported a sudden throughput drop on their Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-us-east-7) starting ~08:10 UTC. Customer sees 3x latency and ~45% lower rps for text-generation routes. No auth/billing errors, just timeouts and 503s from our runtime. Logs attached below.

parth-eng-runtime: thanks. any recent deploys or config changes to that pool? also can you paste a sample of batcher stats (pack sizes, microbatch counts) from around the incident?

ellie-support: no customer-side deploys. We rotated API keys earlier (auth ok). Support log snippet:

```
2026-03-16T08:09:52Z | pool=ded-us-east-7 | route=/v1/complete | status=200 | pack_size_tokens=2048 | batch_count=1
2026-03-16T08:10:03Z | pool=ded-us-east-7 | route=/v1/complete | status=503 | reason=queue_timeout | observed_window_ms=20 | pack_size_tokens=64
2026-03-16T08:10:04Z | pool=ded-us-east-7 | route=/v1/complete | status=504 | reason=infer_timeout | gpu_util=32% | avg_latency_ms=1200
2026-03-16T08:11:00Z | pool=ded-us-east-7 | route=/v1/complete | status=200 | pack_size_tokens=128 | batch_count=5
```

ellie-support: customer says spike began right after we applied a scheduler tuning recommendation to reduce batch_window_ms from 8ms -> 2ms on that pool (attempt to lower tail latency).

parth-eng-runtime: ok that explains a lot — lowering batch_window can fragment work into many small microbatches. Those tiny batches increase kernel overhead and hurt throughput. We need batcher debug output. samir, can you pull queue/batcher metrics? specifically: pack_size_token histogram, microbatch_per_batch, avg_batch_wait_ms, scheduler.quantum, and per-tenant queue depth.

samir-sre: pulling now. hitting internal endpoint to snapshot:

```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_TOKEN" \
  "https://int-api.internal/v1/pools/ded-us-east-7/debug/batcher_snapshot?since=2026-03-16T07:50:00Z" > /tmp/batcher.json
jq '.pack_histogram, .microbatch_counts, .avg_wait_ms, .tenant_queue_depths' /tmp/batcher.json
```

samir-sre: snapshot shows 70% of batches are <= 128 tokens during incident window, microbatch ratio ~4x normal, avg_wait_ms dropped from 7ms->1.8ms, scheduler.quantum is 64 tokens (we lowered it last week). Tenant 42 (acct-acme) is only 22% of requests but is producing many small short sequences and is preempting pack windows leading to packing churn.

parth-eng-runtime: that matches a packing fragmentation story. Two-pronged fix: immediate mitigation + follow-up change. Immediate: restore batch_window_ms to 8ms for that pool and increase scheduler.quantum to 256 so tokens can coalesce. Also temporarily apply per-tenant weight cap to prevent noisy tenant from dominating packing. Natalie, can you push those config flips as a targeted patch to ded-us-east-7?

natalie-ops: will do. preparing a targeted change:

```
PATCH /internal/pools/ded-us-east-7/config
{ "batcher": { "batch_window_ms": 8, "scheduler": { "quantum_tokens": 256 }, "max_batch_tokens": 8192 } }
```

natalie-ops: rolling to 3/3 nodes in the pool now (canary -> remainder). deploy-bot: please gate.

deploy-bot: deploy started for pool ded-us-east-7 config patch (change-id: cfg-20260316-47). canary applied to node-11. monitoring health checks.

natalie-ops: canary passed. rolling to remaining nodes.

parth-eng-runtime: also flagging a longer-term change: we should tweak the scheduler packing heuristics so that when pack_window_ms is low we raise microbatch_penalty and increase unfairness threshold. Otherwise any tenant with many short requests will cause excessive fragmentation. I'll open an RFC/ticket with perf numbers.

samir-sre: after the revert, metrics improved within ~4 minutes: pack_size median jumped from 96->1792 tokens, throughput (rps) recovered ~38%, p95 latency back to pre-incident baseline. No billing/auth anomalies.

ellie-support: customer confirmed recovery on their end and dropped the support case to low priority. they included this note: "Thanks — flipping batch window back fixed our perf. happy to coordinate if you want sample prompts." :thumbsup:

parth-eng-runtime: great. next steps: (1) keep pool at restored values for 24h and monitor packing histograms, (2) add an alert to detect abrupt drop in median pack_size_tokens and auto-suggest/revert aggressive batch_window changes, (3) engineering RFC to add per-tenant small-batch throttles or dynamic window expansion. I'll file the follow-ups.

natalie-ops: filed infra ticket INFRA-4129 and will add a shortrun playbook entry for support folks to check pack hist before recommending batch_window drops.

parth-eng-runtime: thanks all. closing thread after we see stable metrics for 30m. if anyone sees residual 503s/tag me.
